findings.title: Unguarded property access crashes create() for Meet bookings without a destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` can yield `undefined`, but the next line reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. handleNewBooking now passes `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, so `evt.destinationCalendar` becomes `[]`. For a booking with Google Meet location, this throws a TypeError inside create() and the booking fails. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Organization slug and requestedSlug conditions are inverted
findings.body: The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug })`. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` and `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})` (line 153). This flips the logic. With billing disabled (self-hosted), the org is created with no slug. With billing enabled, the slug is written immediately and the requestedSlug approval flow is bypassed. This change is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose and is not mentioned in the description.

findings.title: updateEvent resolves calendarId to undefined when externalCalendarId is empty; deleteEvent falls back to primary
findings.body: The new fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` runs only when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then compares `cal.externalId` against that falsy value, so it matches nothing and returns undefined. The previous code fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. As a result calendarId is undefined and the Google update fails for booking references that have no externalCalendarId. The same bug is at line 317 in deleteEvent: the lookup returns undefined, so deletion silently targets 'primary' and the event remains on the calendar the user actually picked. Fix: select the destination calendar by credential or take the first destination instead of comparing against externalCalendarId.

findings.title: Video references are saved without credentialId, so cancelled video meetings are never deleted
findings.body: The previous code set `credentialId` to `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results. The new code sets it to `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so every video reference is written with credentialId undefined. handleCancelBooking only calls deleteMeeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is truthy (`if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)`). Cancelled bookings will therefore leave the video meeting (Zoom, Daily, Meet, etc.) alive.

findings.title: Office365 and Lark createEvent use the organizer's destination calendar for every credential
findings.body: createEvent takes `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar` and builds the URL from its externalId, ignoring which credential is calling. For collective events, the team member's O365 credential is therefore asked to write to the organizer's calendar id. Graph returns 404 and the member's event is never created. The Lark createEvent (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 128) has the same flaw. The Google implementation avoids this by matching on credentialId. The stated goal, that every host with any calendar app receives the event, is not met for these providers.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent silently creates nothing for team hosts whose calendars don't match the organizer's destination
findings.body: The filter `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` uses the first destination calendar, which belongs to the organizer, even when the call is made with a team member's credential. The team member's CalDAV account has no calendar with that URL, so the filter returns an empty list. responses is then empty, `responses.some((r) => !r.ok)` is false, and createEvent returns a success result with a uid. The member gets no event and no error is surfaced.

findings.title: Destination calendars without credentialId lose their externalId, so events land in primary
findings.body: In the else branch the destination's externalId is dropped: `createEvent(c, event)` is called without it. Google's createEvent resolves the calendar only by matching a destination with the credential's id, so for a legacy destination calendar with no credentialId the event goes to 'primary' instead of the calendar the user selected. The reference then stores externalCalendarId as undefined. The previous code used destinationCalendar.externalId for both the insert and the stored reference.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses an undefined calendarId and its promise is neither awaited nor caught
findings.body: The insert falls back to 'primary' (`selectedCalendar || "primary"`), but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`. When no destination calendar matches the credential, which is common when a user has no destination row, selectedCalendar is undefined. The patch is built with an undefined calendar and is fire-and-forget, so the description never gets the Meet link and the rejection is unhandled. Fix: reuse the same resolved calendar id as the insert.

findings.title: Recurring-cancel deletion runs once per calendar reference, causing duplicate deletes
findings.body: The loop now iterates over every calendar reference, but the recurring branch builds `promises` from the full updatedBookings list and the user's calendar credentials. That block does not depend on the current reference, so with N references every updated booking's event is deleted N times on every calendar. This wastes external API calls and can trigger rate limits. The recurring deletion should run once outside the per-reference loop.

findings.title: Team hosts' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The collective-host calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, which is a silent no-op on null. In that case no host other than the organizer receives the event, even though their calendars are connected. Build the array explicitly (`[...(base ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`) instead of pushing onto a possibly-null value.

findings.title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar changes from object to array without notice
findings.body: The field is part of the webhook payload (see the e2e expectations in apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts). Subscribers that read payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or similar will break. Empty values are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking emits null, while confirm, cancel, and reschedule emit []. For collective events the payload now also includes every host's DestinationCalendar row, with userId, credentialId, and externalId (often the account email for Google). This is a breaking, undocumented API change that also widens the data sent to subscribers.

findings.title: Collective and multi-calendar behaviour changed without tests
findings.body: The PR checklist states no tests were added, yet this change reworks destination-calendar routing across EventManager, the Google/Lark/Office365/CalDAV services, and booking cancel/reschedule. The regressions noted in this review (null-safety on the Meet branch, video credentialId, legacy destination routing, updateLocation references) are the kind of thing unit tests of EventManager would catch. At minimum, existing EventManager tests need to be updated for the array shape.

findings.title: loadUsers error handling leaks Prisma error messages as 400s and masks other failures as 500s
findings.body: The catch block turns any Prisma known-request error into an HttpError 400 using `error.message`, so raw database error text goes to the API client. Any other error, such as a thrown Error from the empty-dynamicUserList check, becomes a generic 500 'Unable to load users', which discards the real cause. Database failures should be a 500 with a generic message, and validation errors should keep their specific messages.

findings.title: updateLocation writes calendar references without credentialId or externalCalendarId
findings.body: CalendarManager.updateEvent does not return credentialId or externalId in its EventResult. The new `credentialId: result.credentialId ?? undefined` and `externalCalendarId: result.externalId` therefore store null for calendar references. The previous code fell back to evt.destinationCalendar. Those references are then used by handleCancelBooking, which takes the legacy path and deletes by uid on every calendar of that type, or targets 'primary' for Google, so the real event is left behind.

findings.title: Reschedule with newBookingId deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: After updating calendar events for all references, the merge path still picks a single old calendar reference with `booking.references.find(...)`. Bookings with several calendar references (the collective multi-host case this PR enables) keep the old events on the other hosts' calendars.

findings.title: Confirming a collective booking never includes team hosts' destination calendars
findings.body: The confirm handler builds evt.destinationCalendar only from the booking's destination or the organizer's. Unlike handleNewBooking, it does not add collective hosts' calendars. Bookings that require confirmation are therefore created only on the organizer's calendar when confirmed. The same gap exists in the Stripe and PayPal payment-success paths, which also build evt from the booking and organizer only.

findings.title: Dynamic-user query drops the organization select without explanation
findings.body: The findMany for dynamic users previously selected `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. That select is removed here with no replacement. Any downstream code that reads users[].organization will get undefined. The change is unrelated to the PR's purpose and should be justified or reverted.
